questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Heating $[Ti(H_2O)_6]Cl_3$ to remove the water makes the substance colourless.
Reason (R): In the absence of ligands, crystal field splitting of the d orbitals does not occur.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true. NCERT states that removing water from $[Ti(H_2O)_6]Cl_3$ on heating renders it colourless.
R is true. Without ligands, the five d orbitals remain degenerate, so they do not split.
R explains A. With no splitting, no d–d transition can absorb visible light, so no colour is seen. The same idea explains why anhydrous $CuSO_4$ is white while $CuSO_4.5H_2O$ is blue.
Answer: (1)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following statements regarding the spectrochemical series and crystal field theory is INCORRECT?
options: $F^-$ produces a smaller crystal field splitting than $H_2O$
Thiocyanate bonded through nitrogen ($NCS^-$) is a stronger field ligand than when bonded through sulphur ($SCN^-$)
Experimentally, anionic ligands are found at the high end of the series, as expected from treating ligands as point charges
The spectrochemical series is determined experimentally from the absorption of light by complexes
questions.explanation:
(1) Correct: in the series, $F^-$ comes before (is weaker than) $H_2O$.
(2) Correct: $SCN^-$ lies near the weak end, while $NCS^-$ lies after $H_2O$.
(3) Incorrect: the point-charge model predicts that anionic ligands should split the d orbitals most, but they are actually found at the low end. This is a recognised limitation of CFT.
(4) Correct: the series is based on absorption spectra.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Match the neutral ligands in List-I with the names used for them in coordination compounds in List-II.
List-I
(a) $NH_3$
(b) $H_2O$
(c) $CO$
(d) $NO$
List-II
(i) carbonyl
(ii) nitrosyl
(iii) ammine
(iv) aqua
questions.explanation:
Neutral ligands normally keep their molecular names. NCERT lists four special exceptions.
(a) $NH_3$ is ammine. It is spelt with double m, unlike the amine of organic chemistry.
(b) $H_2O$ is aqua.
(c) $CO$ is carbonyl.
(d) $NO$ is nitrosyl.
Option (3) swaps carbonyl and nitrosyl, so it is wrong.
Answer: (1)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Match List-I (metal carbonyl) with List-II (structure):
List-I
(A) $Ni(CO)_4$
(B) $Fe(CO)_5$
(C) $Cr(CO)_6$
(D) $Mn_2(CO)_{10}$
List-II
(i) Octahedral
(ii) Two square pyramidal units joined by a metal–metal bond
(iii) Tetrahedral
(iv) Trigonal bipyramidal
questions.explanation:
(A) Tetracarbonylnickel(0) is tetrahedral, so A-iii.
(B) Pentacarbonyliron(0) is trigonal bipyramidal, so B-iv.
(C) Hexacarbonylchromium(0) is octahedral, so C-i.
(D) Decacarbonyldimanganese(0) is two square pyramidal $Mn(CO)_5$ units joined by an Mn–Mn bond, so D-ii.
Answer: (1)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Match List-I (pair of compounds) with List-II (type of isomerism).
List-I:
(A) $[Co(NH_3)_5(SO_4)]Br$ and $[Co(NH_3)_5Br]SO_4$
(B) $[Cr(H_2O)_6]Cl_3$ and $[Cr(H_2O)_5Cl]Cl_2.H_2O$
(C) $[Co(NH_3)_6][Cr(CN)_6]$ and $[Cr(NH_3)_6][Co(CN)_6]$
(D) Red and yellow forms of $[Co(NH_3)_5(NO_2)]Cl_2$
List-II:
(I) Linkage
(II) Coordination
(III) Solvate (hydrate)
(IV) Ionisation
questions.explanation:
(A) The counter ion and a ligand swap places ($SO_4^{2-}$ and $Br^-$), so this is ionisation isomerism (IV).
(B) Water is coordinated in one isomer and present as lattice water in the other, so this is solvate (hydrate) isomerism (III).
(C) Ligands are interchanged between the cationic and anionic entities, so this is coordination isomerism (II).
(D) Nitrite binds through O (red form) or through N (yellow form), so this is linkage isomerism (I).
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: In the compound K$_4$[Fe(CN)$_6$], the counter ion is:
questions.explanation:
The central atom and its ligands, enclosed in square brackets, form the coordination sphere. Here that is [Fe(CN)$_6$]$^{4-}$.
The ionisable groups written outside the bracket are the counter ions. Here the counter ion is K$^+$.
CN$^-$ is a ligand and Fe$^{2+}$ is the central ion; neither is a counter ion.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: 2.665 g of the grey-green hydrate isomer $[Cr(H_2O)_5Cl]Cl_2\cdot H_2O$ is dissolved in water and treated with excess $AgNO_3$ solution in the cold. What mass of AgCl is precipitated? (Atomic masses: Cr = 52, Cl = 35.5, O = 16, H = 1, Ag = 108)
questions.explanation:
Given: molar mass of $CrCl_3\cdot 6H_2O$ = 52 + 3(35.5) + 6(18) = 266.5 g/mol.
Moles of complex = 2.665/266.5 = 0.01 mol.
Only the two $Cl^-$ ions outside the bracket are ionisable, so 1 mol of complex gives 2 mol AgCl. Moles of AgCl = 0.02 mol.
Substituting: mass = 0.02 × 143.5 = 2.87 g.
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following cobalt(III) complexes absorbs light in the ultraviolet region (around 310 nm) rather than the visible region, and therefore appears only pale yellow?
questions.explanation:
$CN^-$ is very high in the spectrochemical series. It produces a very large $\Delta_o$.
A larger splitting needs higher-energy, shorter-wavelength light, here about 310 nm in the UV region.
So $[Co(CN)_6]^{3-}$ is only pale yellow.
$[Co(NH_3)_6]^{3+}$ is the tempting choice, but it absorbs at 475 nm (visible) and appears orange.
The Cl- and $H_2O$-containing complexes absorb at even longer wavelengths (535 nm and 500 nm).
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: $[Co(NH_3)_6]^{3+}$ is diamagnetic and octahedral. On the basis of valence bond theory, it is best described as:
options: an outer orbital, high spin complex using $sp^3d^2$ hybridisation
an inner orbital, low spin complex using $d^2sp^3$ hybridisation
an inner orbital, high spin complex using $d^2sp^3$ hybridisation
an outer orbital, low spin complex using $sp^3d^2$ hybridisation
questions.explanation:
Co$^{3+}$ is $3d^6$. In this complex the six d electrons pair up in three 3d orbitals, which leaves two inner 3d orbitals vacant.
These two 3d orbitals mix with 4s and 4p to give $d^2sp^3$ hybrid orbitals. Because inner (3d) orbitals are used, the complex is called inner orbital, low spin or spin paired. It is diamagnetic.
Option (1) describes $[CoF_6]^{3-}$, which uses 4d orbitals and is paramagnetic.
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Statement I: As water ligands in $[Ni(H_2O)_6]^{2+}$ are successively replaced by ethane-1,2-diamine to finally give $[Ni(en)_3]^{2+}$, the wavelength of light absorbed by the complex progressively decreases.
Statement II: en lies above $H_2O$ in the spectrochemical series, so replacing $H_2O$ by en increases $\Delta_o$.
Choose the correct option.
options: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both statements are correct and Statement II correctly explains Statement I
Both statements are correct but Statement II does not explain Statement I
questions.explanation:
Statement II is correct. In the series … $H_2O$ < NCS$^-$ < edta$^{4-}$ < $NH_3$ < en …, en is a stronger-field ligand than water.
Statement I is correct. Each replacement raises $\Delta_o$, so a higher-energy (shorter-wavelength) photon is needed for the d-d transition.
This matches the observed colour change from green to violet: the absorbed light moves from the red end towards yellow.
Statement II is the cause of Statement I, so it correctly explains it.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Match List-I (chelating agent / drug) with List-II (medicinal use).
List-I:
(A) D-penicillamine
(B) Desferrioxime B
(C) EDTA
(D) cis-platin
List-II:
(I) Treatment of lead poisoning
(II) Inhibits growth of tumours
(III) Removal of excess copper
(IV) Removal of excess iron
questions.explanation:
A-III: D-penicillamine is a chelating ligand that removes excess copper.
B-IV: Desferrioxime B is a chelating ligand that removes excess iron.
C-I: EDTA is used to treat lead poisoning.
D-II: cis-platin and related platinum compounds inhibit the growth of tumours.
Answer: (1)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Assertion (A): In the name pentaamminenitrito-N-cobalt(III) chloride for the yellow form of $[Co(NH_3)_5(NO_2)]Cl_2$, the symbol N must be included after 'nitrito'.
Reason (R): The nitrite ion is an ambidentate ligand that can bind to the metal either through nitrogen or through oxygen.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
R is true: $NO_2^-$ is ambidentate. It can bind as M–NO₂ (through N) or as M–ONO (through O).
A is true: the yellow form contains N-bonded nitrite, and the red form contains O-bonded nitrite. Writing nitrito-N or nitrito-O makes the name unambiguous for these linkage isomers.
The need to specify the donor atom arises precisely because the ligand is ambidentate. So R correctly explains A.
Answer: (1)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: A coordination entity absorbs light of wavelength 600 nm, which lies in the red region of the visible spectrum. The colour of the entity, as listed for $[Cu(H_2O)_4]^{2+}$ in NCERT, is:
questions.explanation:
The colour of a complex is complementary to the colour of light it absorbs. We see the wavelengths that are left over.
$[Cu(H_2O)_4]^{2+}$ absorbs red light (600 nm), so it appears blue.
'Red' is the most tempting wrong option. It is the colour that is absorbed, not the colour that is seen.
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: For a certain metal ion with a given set of ligands, the octahedral crystal field splitting is $\Delta_o = 18000\ \text{cm}^{-1}$. What is the expected tetrahedral splitting $\Delta_t$ for the same metal, the same ligands and the same metal–ligand distance?
questions.explanation:
Given: $\Delta_o = 18000\ \text{cm}^{-1}$.
Formula: $\Delta_t = \frac{4}{9}\Delta_o$ (same metal, same ligands, same distance).
Substituting: $\Delta_t = \frac{4}{9} \times 18000 = 8000\ \text{cm}^{-1}$.
So $\Delta_t = 8000\ \text{cm}^{-1}$. The value 40500 cm$^{-1}$ comes from wrongly multiplying by 9/4.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 5 · Coordination Compounds

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Linkage isomerism in coordination compounds is possible only when the complex contains
options: a counter ion that can also act as a ligand
solvent molecules in the crystal lattice
questions.explanation:
Linkage isomerism arises when a ligand has two different donor atoms and can bind through either of them. Such a ligand is called ambidentate, for example $NO_2^-$ (N or O) and $SCN^-$ (S or N).
A counter ion that can act as a ligand leads to ionisation isomerism, not linkage isomerism.
Solvent molecules in the lattice lead to solvate isomerism.
Chelating ligands do not by themselves produce linkage isomers.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 5 · Coordination Compounds

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Erdmann's salt has the formula $NH_4[Co(NH_3)_2(NO_2)_4]$, with each nitrite ligand bonded through nitrogen. What is its correct IUPAC name?
questions.explanation:
Step 1: The cation $NH_4^+$ is named first. The complex is therefore an anion of charge −1.
Step 2: Find the oxidation state: $x + 2(0) + 4(-1) = -1$, so Co = +3.
Step 3: Ligands go in alphabetical order. Ammine (a) comes before nitrito (n), and the multiplier prefixes are ignored. Since the nitrite is N-bonded, it is written nitrito-N.
Step 4: Because the complex is an anion, cobalt becomes cobaltate.
Option (1) has the wrong ligand order, option (2) misses -ate, and option (3) has the wrong oxidation state.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 5 · Coordination Compounds

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The compound $[Pt(NH_3)_4][CuCl_4]$ contains both a complex cation and a complex anion. Its correct IUPAC name is:
questions.explanation:
Step 1: $NH_3$ is neutral, so the cation $[Pt(NH_3)_4]^{n+}$ has a charge equal to the oxidation state of Pt.
Step 2: In $[CuCl_4]^{m-}$, the charge equals $4 - y$, where y is the oxidation state of Cu.
Step 3: The compound must be neutral, so the two charges are equal. The usual +2 states give $[Pt(NH_3)_4]^{2+}$ and $[CuCl_4]^{2-}$.
Step 4: The cation is named first, with the metal as platinum. The anion takes the Latin root plus –ate, giving cuprate.
Option (1) puts the suffixes on the wrong ions. Option (4) names the anion first.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 5 · Coordination Compounds

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: In an octahedral crystal field, which pair of d orbitals is raised in energy because its lobes point along the axes towards the approaching ligands?
questions.explanation:
In an octahedral entity the six ligands lie along the x, y and z axes.
The $d_{x^2-y^2}$ and $d_{z^2}$ orbitals point along these axes, so they are repelled more strongly and rise in energy. Together they form the $e_g$ set.
The $d_{xy}$, $d_{yz}$ and $d_{xz}$ orbitals point between the axes, so they are lowered in energy. They form the $t_{2g}$ set.
Options mixing one axial orbital with one between-axes orbital are therefore wrong.
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a double salt?
questions.explanation:
Double salts dissociate completely into simple ions in water. Carnallite, Mohr's salt and potash alum all behave this way.
K$_4$[Fe(CN)$_6$] is a complex. Its ion [Fe(CN)$_6$]$^{4-}$ does not break up into Fe$^{2+}$ and CN$^-$ ions.
Answer: (4)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: cis-Platin, cis-$[PtCl_2(NH_3)_2]$, is used to inhibit the growth of tumours. Which of the following statements about it is INCORRECT?
options: Platinum is in the +2 oxidation state
It is square planar, involves $dsp^2$ hybridisation and is diamagnetic
It shows geometrical isomerism, and its isomer is the trans form
The cis isomer is optically active because its two Cl ligands are adjacent
questions.explanation:
(1) Correct: NH3 is neutral and the two Cl contribute $-2$, so Pt is +2 ($5d^8$).
(2) Correct: a square planar d8 complex uses $dsp^2$ hybridisation, and its electrons are paired, so it is diamagnetic (compare $[Pt(CN)_4]^{2-}$).
(3) Correct: an $[MX_2L_2]$ square planar complex has cis and trans forms (Fig. 5.2).
(4) Incorrect: the molecular plane of a square planar complex is a plane of symmetry, so its mirror image can be superimposed. It is therefore not optically active.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 5 · Coordination Compounds

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following statements is INCORRECT?
options: $[Co(NH_3)_5Br]SO_4$ and $[Co(NH_3)_5(SO_4)]Br$ each furnish two ions per formula unit in aqueous solution
Cobalt has the oxidation state +3 in both $[Co(NH_3)_5Br]SO_4$ and $[Co(NH_3)_5(SO_4)]Br$
In the grey-green isomer $[Cr(H_2O)_5Cl]Cl_2\cdot H_2O$, the coordination number of chromium is 5
In both $[Co(NH_3)_6][Cr(CN)_6]$ and its coordination isomer, each metal is in the +3 oxidation state
questions.explanation:
(1) Correct: the first gives $[Co(NH_3)_5Br]^{2+}$ + $SO_4^{2-}$, and the second gives $[Co(NH_3)_5SO_4]^+$ + $Br^-$. Each yields two ions.
(2) Correct: for the first, x − 1 = +2, so x = +3. For the second, x − 2 = +1, so x = +3.
(3) Incorrect: Cr is bonded to 5 $H_2O$ and 1 $Cl^-$, so its coordination number is 6. The lattice water is not counted.
(4) Correct: the complexes are $[Co(NH_3)_6]^{3+}$, $[Cr(CN)_6]^{3-}$, $[Cr(NH_3)_6]^{3+}$ and $[Co(CN)_6]^{3-}$, so every metal is +3.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 5 · Coordination Compounds

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: In an octahedral crystal field, which set of d orbitals is raised in energy above the average energy of the spherical field?
questions.explanation:
In an octahedral complex, the six ligands lie along the x, y and z axes.
The $d_{x^2-y^2}$ and $d_{z^2}$ orbitals point along these axes, directly at the ligands. They feel more repulsion and rise in energy, forming the $e_g$ set.
$d_{xy}$, $d_{yz}$ and $d_{xz}$ point between the axes. They are lowered in energy and form the $t_{2g}$ set, so option (1) is the wrong set.
Option (4) mixes one orbital from each set.
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Assertion (A): The green and violet forms of CoCl$_3$.4NH$_3$ each give 1 mol AgCl per mole with excess AgNO$_3$, yet they show distinct properties.
Reason (R): Both are isomers containing the same coordination entity [CoCl$_2$(NH$_3$)$_4$]$^+$, differing only in the spatial arrangement of the two chloride ligands.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true. Both forms behave as 1:1 electrolytes and precipitate 1 mol AgCl, but they differ in colour and other properties.
R is true. Both are [CoCl$_2$(NH$_3$)$_4$]Cl. The two Cl ligands can be cis or trans to each other, so the two forms are isomers.
This isomerism explains why compounds with the same empirical formula and the same ionisable chloride behave differently, so R explains A.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 5 · Coordination Compounds

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following statements about Werner's theory of coordination compounds is INCORRECT?
options: Primary valences are normally ionisable and are satisfied by negative ions.
Secondary valences are ionisable and can be satisfied only by neutral molecules.
The secondary valence equals the coordination number and is fixed for a metal.
Groups bound by secondary linkages have characteristic spatial arrangements for different coordination numbers.
questions.explanation:
(1) Correct: primary valences are ionisable and are satisfied by anions.
(2) Incorrect: secondary valences are non-ionisable. They can be satisfied by neutral molecules OR negative ions. For example, $Cl^-$ satisfies a secondary valence in $[CoCl(NH_3)_5]^{2+}$.
(3) Correct: the secondary valence equals the coordination number and is fixed for a metal.
(4) Correct: these spatial arrangements are called coordination polyhedra in modern terms.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 5 · Coordination Compounds

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
How many of the following species are chiral?
$[Co(en)_3]^{3+}$, cis-$[CoCl_2(en)_2]^{+}$, trans-$[CoCl_2(en)_2]^{+}$, $[Cr(C_2O_4)_3]^{3-}$, cis-$[Pt(NH_3)_2Cl_2]$, fac-$[Co(NH_3)_3(NO_2)_3]$, cis-$[CrCl_2(ox)_2]^{3-}$, $[Ni(CO)_4]$
questions.explanation:
Chiral species:
- $[Co(en)_3]^{3+}$: three chelate rings in a propeller arrangement.
- cis-$[CoCl_2(en)_2]^{+}$
- $[Cr(C_2O_4)_3]^{3-}$
- cis-$[CrCl_2(ox)_2]^{3-}$

Achiral species:
- trans-$[CoCl_2(en)_2]^{+}$: has a mirror plane.
- cis-$[Pt(NH_3)_2Cl_2]$: planar.
- fac-$[Co(NH_3)_3(NO_2)_3]$: has mirror planes.
- $[Ni(CO)_4]$: homoleptic tetrahedral.

Count of chiral species = 4.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Statement I: Valence bond theory does not distinguish between weak field and strong field ligands.
Statement II: Valence bond theory gives a quantitative interpretation of the magnetic data of coordination compounds.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Statement I: Correct. NCERT lists 'does not distinguish between weak and strong ligands' as a limitation of VBT.
Statement II: Incorrect. Another limitation of VBT is that it does not give a quantitative interpretation of magnetic data. It also fails to explain colour.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
How many of the following coordination entities are homoleptic?
$[Co(NH_3)_6]^{3+}$, $[Ni(CO)_4]$, $[Co(NH_3)_4Cl_2]^+$, $[Fe(CN)_6]^{4-}$, $[PtCl_2(NH_3)_2]$, $[Co(en)_3]^{3+}$
questions.explanation:
A homoleptic complex has the metal bound to only one kind of donor group.
(i) $[Co(NH_3)_6]^{3+}$: only $NH_3$, so homoleptic.
(ii) $[Ni(CO)_4]$: only CO, so homoleptic.
(iii) $[Co(NH_3)_4Cl_2]^+$: $NH_3$ and $Cl^-$, so heteroleptic.
(iv) $[Fe(CN)_6]^{4-}$: only $CN^-$, so homoleptic.
(v) $[PtCl_2(NH_3)_2]$: two kinds of ligand, so heteroleptic.
(vi) $[Co(en)_3]^{3+}$: only en, so homoleptic.
The total is 4.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
$[Ti(H_2O)_6]^{3+}$ shows its d-d absorption maximum at 498 nm. Find the crystal field splitting energy $\Delta_o$ in kJ/mol.
(Use $h = 6.626 \times 10^{-34}$ J s, $c = 3.0 \times 10^{8}$ m/s, $N_A = 6.022 \times 10^{23}$ mol$^{-1}$.)
questions.explanation:
Given: $\lambda = 498$ nm $= 498 \times 10^{-9}$ m. The absorbed photon promotes the electron $t_{2g} \rightarrow e_g$, so its energy equals $\Delta_o$.
Formula: $\Delta_o = \frac{hcN_A}{\lambda}$.
Substituting: energy per ion $= \frac{6.626\times10^{-34}\times3.0\times10^{8}}{498\times10^{-9}} = 3.99\times10^{-19}$ J.
Per mole: $3.99\times10^{-19}\times6.022\times10^{23} = 2.404\times10^{5}$ J/mol.
So $\Delta_o \approx 240.4$ kJ/mol.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 5 · Coordination Compounds

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Assertion (A): $[Mn(CN)_6]^{3-}$ is an inner orbital complex, yet it is paramagnetic.
Reason (R): In $d^2sp^3$ hybridisation, all the 3d electrons of the metal ion must be paired.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true. $Mn^{3+}$ is $3d^4$. Pairing frees two 3d orbitals for $d^2sp^3$ hybridisation. The 4 electrons then sit in three 3d orbitals, which leaves 2 unpaired electrons, so the complex is paramagnetic.
R is false. $d^2sp^3$ only requires two vacant 3d orbitals. Unpaired electrons can remain, as in $[Mn(CN)_6]^{3-}$ (2 unpaired) and $[Fe(CN)_6]^{3-}$ (1 unpaired).
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 5 · Coordination Compounds

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Assertion (A): For a $d^4$ ion in an octahedral field with $\Delta_o < P$, the electronic configuration is $t_{2g}^{3}e_g^{1}$.
Reason (R): When $\Delta_o < P$, placing the fourth electron in an $e_g$ orbital costs less energy than pairing it in a $t_{2g}$ orbital.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
The fourth electron has two choices. It can pair in $t_{2g}$, which costs the pairing energy P. Or it can enter $e_g$, which costs the splitting energy $\Delta_o$.
If $\Delta_o < P$, entering $e_g$ is cheaper. This gives $t_{2g}^{3}e_g^{1}$, a high-spin configuration with weak field ligands, so A is true.
R states exactly this energy comparison, so R is true and it explains A.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 5 · Coordination Compounds

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Ethane-1,2-diamine (en) is added step by step to an aqueous solution of $[Ni(H_2O)_6]^{2+}$ in en:Ni molar ratios 1:1, 2:1 and 3:1. Which sequence correctly gives the colours of $[Ni(H_2O)_6]^{2+}$, $[Ni(H_2O)_4(en)]^{2+}$, $[Ni(H_2O)_2(en)_2]^{2+}$ and $[Ni(en)_3]^{2+}$, in that order?
questions.explanation:
Each en ligand replaces two water molecules. The NCERT reaction sequence gives these colours:
$[Ni(H_2O)_6]^{2+}$: green.
$[Ni(H_2O)_4(en)]^{2+}$: pale blue.
$[Ni(H_2O)_2(en)_2]^{2+}$: blue/purple.
$[Ni(en)_3]^{2+}$: violet.
Option (1) gives the same colours but in the reverse order, which is the common trap.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 5 · Coordination Compounds

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Assertion (A): $[Co(NH_3)_4Cl_2]^+$ exists as two geometrical isomers.
Reason (R): In an octahedral complex of type $[MX_2L_4]$, the two X ligands can be placed either at $90^\circ$ or at $180^\circ$ to each other.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true. $[Co(NH_3)_4Cl_2]^+$ has cis and trans forms (NCERT Fig. 5.3).
R is true. In an octahedron, two positions are either adjacent ($90^\circ$, cis) or opposite ($180^\circ$, trans).
These are the only two distinct arrangements, so there are exactly two isomers.
R therefore directly explains A.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 5 · Coordination Compounds

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
How many of the following statements are correct?
(i) $[Ni(CO)_4]$ is tetrahedral.
(ii) $[Cr(CO)_6]$ is octahedral.
(iii) In $[Mn_2(CO)_{10}]$, each $Mn(CO)_5$ unit is trigonal bipyramidal.
(iv) $[Co_2(CO)_8]$ has a Co–Co bond bridged by two CO groups.
(v) The M–C $\sigma$ bond in carbonyls is formed by donation of the lone pair on the oxygen atom of CO.
questions.explanation:
(i) Correct: $[Ni(CO)_4]$ is tetrahedral.
(ii) Correct: $[Cr(CO)_6]$ is octahedral.
(iii) Incorrect: each $Mn(CO)_5$ unit is square pyramidal, not trigonal bipyramidal.
(iv) Correct: the Co–Co bond in $[Co_2(CO)_8]$ is bridged by two CO groups.
(v) Incorrect: the $\sigma$ donation comes from the lone pair on carbon, not oxygen.
So three statements are correct.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 5 · Coordination Compounds

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Statement I: In a tetrahedral crystal field, the d orbitals split in the same order as in an octahedral field; only the magnitude of splitting is smaller.
Statement II: The subscript 'g' is not used for the d-orbital energy levels in a tetrahedral field because tetrahedral complexes lack a centre of symmetry.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
questions.explanation:
Statement I is incorrect. Tetrahedral splitting is inverted compared with octahedral splitting: the two-orbital set lies lower and the three-orbital set lies higher. It is also smaller in magnitude, with $\Delta_t = \frac{4}{9}\Delta_o$.
Statement II is correct. The label 'g' is used only for complexes that have a centre of symmetry, such as octahedral and square planar complexes. Tetrahedral complexes have no centre of symmetry.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 5 · Coordination Compounds

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Assertion (A): $[Co(NH_3)_5(SO_4)]Br$ and $[Co(NH_3)_5Br]SO_4$ are ionisation isomers.
Reason (R): Ionisation isomerism arises when the counter ion of a complex salt is itself a potential ligand and can displace a ligand, which then becomes the counter ion.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true. Both compounds have the same formula, $CoN_5H_{15}SO_4Br$. They give different ions in solution: $Br^-$ in one and $SO_4^{2-}$ in the other.
R is true. It is the NCERT definition of ionisation isomerism.
R directly explains A: sulphate and bromide simply exchange their roles as ligand and counter ion.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 5 · Coordination Compounds

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Match List-I (ligand) with List-II (description):
List-I
(A) $EDTA^{4-}$
(B) $H_2NCH_2CH_2NH_2$
(C) $NO_2^-$
(D) $N(CH_2CH_2NH_2)_3$
List-II
(p) Hexadentate
(q) Didentate
(r) Ambidentate
(s) Tetradentate (polydentate)
questions.explanation:
(A) $EDTA^{4-}$ binds through 2 N and 4 O atoms, so it is hexadentate: (p).
(B) Ethane-1,2-diamine binds through two N atoms, so it is didentate: (q).
(C) $NO_2^-$ can bind through either N or O, so it is ambidentate: (r).
(D) $N(CH_2CH_2NH_2)_3$ has four N donor atoms, so it is a tetradentate (polydentate) ligand: (s).
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 5 · Coordination Compounds

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: For an octahedral $d^6$ complex, $\Delta_o = 22000\ cm^{-1}$ and the pairing energy is $P = 17000\ cm^{-1}$. Take the $t_{2g}$ level at $-0.4\Delta_o$ and the $e_g$ level at $+0.6\Delta_o$, and add P for every electron pair. By how much is the low-spin configuration lower in energy than the high-spin configuration?
questions.explanation:
High spin is $t_{2g}^{4}e_g^{2}$: $4(-0.4\Delta_o) + 2(0.6\Delta_o) = -0.4\Delta_o$. It has 1 electron pair, so its energy is $-0.4(22000) + 17000 = 8200\ cm^{-1}$.
Low spin is $t_{2g}^{6}e_g^{0}$: $6(-0.4\Delta_o) = -2.4\Delta_o$. It has 3 electron pairs, so its energy is $-52800 + 51000 = -1800\ cm^{-1}$.
Difference: $8200 - (-1800) = 10000\ cm^{-1}$, which also equals $2\Delta_o - 2P$.
Option (1) ignores pairing energy. Option (2) counts only one extra pair.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 5 · Coordination Compounds

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
How many of the following show geometrical isomerism?
$[Pt(NH_3)_2Cl_2]$ (square planar), $[Co(NH_3)_5Cl]^{2+}$, $[CoCl_2(en)_2]^+$, $[Co(NH_3)_3(NO_2)_3]$, $[Zn(NH_3)_2Cl_2]$ (tetrahedral), $[Fe(NH_3)_2(CN)_4]^-$, $[Co(en)_3]^{3+}$
questions.explanation:
$[Pt(NH_3)_2Cl_2]$: yes, it is square planar $MX_2L_2$ with cis and trans forms.
$[Co(NH_3)_5Cl]^{2+}$: no. With a single Cl, all its positions are equivalent.
$[CoCl_2(en)_2]^+$: yes, it has cis and trans forms.
$[Co(NH_3)_3(NO_2)_3]$: yes, it has fac and mer forms.
$[Zn(NH_3)_2Cl_2]$: no, because it is tetrahedral.
$[Fe(NH_3)_2(CN)_4]^-$: yes, it is $MX_2L_4$ with cis and trans forms.
$[Co(en)_3]^{3+}$: no geometrical isomers; it shows only optical isomerism.
Count = 4.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 5 · Coordination Compounds

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: $[FeF_6]^{3-}$ and $[Fe(CN)_6]^{3-}$ are both octahedral Fe(III) complexes. Using magnetic data consistent with NCERT, by how much does the spin-only magnetic moment of $[FeF_6]^{3-}$ exceed that of $[Fe(CN)_6]^{3-}$? (Use $\mu = \sqrt{n(n+2)}$ BM.)
questions.explanation:
Given: $Fe^{3+}$ is $3d^5$. $F^-$ is a weak field ligand, so $[FeF_6]^{3-}$ has n = 5. $CN^-$ is a strong field ligand, so $[Fe(CN)_6]^{3-}$ has n = 1.
Formula: $\mu = \sqrt{n(n+2)}$ BM.
Substituting: for n = 5, $\mu = \sqrt{35} = 5.92$ BM. For n = 1, $\mu = \sqrt{3} = 1.73$ BM.
So the difference is 5.92 − 1.73 = 4.19 BM.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 5 · Coordination Compounds

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Jørgensen obtained the complex $[Co(NH_3)_5(NO_2)]Cl_2$ in a red form and a yellow form. In the red form, the nitrite ligand is attached to cobalt through
options: both nitrogen and oxygen, as a chelate
the chloride ion, which displaces nitrite
questions.explanation:
NCERT states that the red form has nitrite bound through oxygen ($-ONO$, nitrito-O).
The yellow form has nitrite bound through nitrogen ($-NO_2$, nitrito-N).
Nitrite is ambidentate, not didentate, so it binds through only one atom at a time. A chelate option is therefore wrong.
Option (1) describes the yellow form, which makes it the tempting trap.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 5 · Coordination Compounds

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Match List-I (complex) with List-II (d-electron configuration in the octahedral field).
List-I:
(A) $[Ti(H_2O)_6]^{3+}$
(B) $[Co(NH_3)_6]^{3+}$
(C) $[FeF_6]^{3-}$
(D) $[Fe(CN)_6]^{3-}$
List-II:
(i) $t_{2g}^{3}e_g^{2}$
(ii) $t_{2g}^{5}e_g^{0}$
(iii) $t_{2g}^{1}e_g^{0}$
(iv) $t_{2g}^{6}e_g^{0}$
questions.explanation:
(A) $Ti^{3+}$ is $d^1$, so its single electron sits in $t_{2g}$: $t_{2g}^{1}e_g^{0}$, which is (iii).
(B) $Co^{3+}$ is $d^6$. $NH_3$ causes pairing, as shown by the diamagnetic complex: $t_{2g}^{6}e_g^{0}$, which is (iv).
(C) $Fe^{3+}$ is $d^5$. $F^-$ is a weak field ligand, giving high spin with five unpaired electrons: $t_{2g}^{3}e_g^{2}$, which is (i).
(D) $Fe^{3+}$ is $d^5$. $CN^-$ is a strong field ligand, giving one unpaired electron: $t_{2g}^{5}e_g^{0}$, which is (ii).
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 5 · Coordination Compounds

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Consider the dinuclear carbonyls $[Mn_2(CO)_{10}]$ and $[Co_2(CO)_8]$ as described in NCERT. What is the total number of terminal (non-bridging) CO groups in one molecule of each, taken together?
questions.explanation:
Step 1: In $[Mn_2(CO)_{10}]$, two $Mn(CO)_5$ units are joined only by a Mn–Mn bond. There is no bridging CO, so all 10 CO groups are terminal.
Step 2: In $[Co_2(CO)_8]$, the Co–Co bond is bridged by 2 CO groups. The remaining $8 - 2 = 6$ CO groups are terminal.
Step 3: Total terminal CO groups $= 10 + 6 = 16$.
Option (1), 18, results from wrongly treating every CO as terminal.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 5 · Coordination Compounds

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following statements about writing formulas of mononuclear coordination entities is INCORRECT?
options: The symbol of the central atom is written first inside the square bracket.
Anionic ligands are always listed before neutral ligands, whatever their alphabetical order.
Formulas of polyatomic ligands are enclosed in parentheses.
The charge of an entity written without its counter ion is shown as a right superscript outside the square bracket, number before sign.
questions.explanation:
(1) Correct: the central atom is listed first.
(2) Incorrect: ligands are listed in alphabetical order. The position of a ligand does not depend on its charge.
(3) Correct: an example is $[Co(NH_3)_6]^{3+}$.
(4) Correct: an example is $[Co(CN)_6]^{3-}$.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 5 · Coordination Compounds

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Consider the octahedral ion $[Co(NH_3)_2Cl_2(en)]^{+}$. Which of the following statements are correct?
(i) It has three geometrical isomers.
(ii) The isomer in which the two Cl ligands are trans to each other is optically inactive.
(iii) The isomer in which the two $NH_3$ ligands are trans to each other is chiral.
(iv) The total number of stereoisomers is 4.
questions.explanation:
en must span two cis positions.
(i) Correct. The three arrangements are: Cl trans; $NH_3$ trans; and all cis.
(ii) Correct. With Cl trans, the en ring and both $NH_3$ lie in one plane, which is a mirror plane, so the isomer is achiral.
(iii) Incorrect. With $NH_3$ trans, the plane containing en and both Cl is a mirror plane, so this isomer is also achiral.
(iv) Correct. Only the all-cis isomer is chiral, giving d and l forms. Total = 2 + 2 = 4.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 5 · Coordination Compounds

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the octahedral complex $[Ni(NH_3)_6]^{2+}$ is INCORRECT?
options: Nickel is in the +2 oxidation state with a $3d^8$ configuration.
Even if all the 3d electrons pair up, two vacant 3d orbitals cannot be obtained, so 4d orbitals are used.
It is paramagnetic with two unpaired electrons, giving a spin-only moment of about 2.83 BM.
Like $[Co(NH_3)_6]^{3+}$, it is a $d^2sp^3$ inner orbital complex.
questions.explanation:
(1) Correct: $NH_3$ is neutral, so Ni is +2, which is $3d^8$.
(2) Correct: 8 electrons need at least four 3d orbitals even when fully paired. Only one 3d orbital can be vacated, so two cannot be freed, and the complex uses $sp^3d^2$ with outer 4d orbitals.
(3) Correct: two unpaired electrons give $\mu = \sqrt{8} \approx 2.83$ BM.
(4) Incorrect: it is an outer orbital complex, unlike $d^6$ $[Co(NH_3)_6]^{3+}$.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 5 · Coordination Compounds

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: 0.005 mol of a cobalt(III) complex of empirical formula CoCl$_3$.xNH$_3$ (coordination number of Co = 6) is treated with excess AgNO$_3$ solution in the cold, and 1.435 g of AgCl is precipitated. What is the value of x? (Atomic masses: Ag = 108, Cl = 35.5)
questions.explanation:
Given: n(complex) = 0.005 mol; mass of AgCl = 1.435 g; M(AgCl) = 143.5 g/mol.
n(AgCl) = 1.435/143.5 = 0.01 mol, so each mole of complex has 2 ionisable Cl$^-$.
Coordinated Cl = 3 − 2 = 1, so the number of NH$_3$ = 6 − 1 = 5.
The complex is [CoCl(NH$_3$)$_5$]Cl$_2$, so x = 5.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 5 · Coordination Compounds

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following is a heteroleptic complex?
questions.explanation:
A heteroleptic complex has the metal bound to more than one kind of donor group. A homoleptic complex has only one kind.
$[PtCl_2(NH_3)_2]$ contains two kinds of ligand, $Cl^-$ and $NH_3$, so it is heteroleptic.
The other three each contain a single ligand type ($NH_3$, en or CO), so they are homoleptic.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 5 · Coordination Compounds

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Statement I: In $[Ni(CO)_4]$, nickel is in the zero oxidation state, and the complex is tetrahedral and diamagnetic.
Statement II: Greater $\pi$ back-donation from the metal into the $\pi^*$ orbital of CO increases the C–O bond order, so the C–O bond in a metal carbonyl is shorter than in free CO.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Statement I is correct. NCERT states that $[Ni(CO)_4]$ is tetrahedral and diamagnetic, with Ni(0) having no unpaired electron.
Statement II is incorrect. Back-donation places electrons in the antibonding $\pi^*$ orbital of CO.
Electrons in an antibonding orbital lower the C–O bond order. So the C–O bond becomes longer and weaker, not shorter, even as the M–C bond is strengthened.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 5 · Coordination Compounds

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Assertion (A): $[Co(CN)_6]^{3-}$ absorbs at about 310 nm, whereas $[Co(NH_3)_6]^{3+}$ absorbs at about 475 nm.
Reason (R): $CN^-$ lies higher than $NH_3$ in the spectrochemical series, so it produces a larger crystal field splitting $\Delta_o$ for $Co^{3+}$.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true. The NCERT table lists absorption at 310 nm (ultraviolet) for $[Co(CN)_6]^{3-}$ and at 475 nm (blue) for $[Co(NH_3)_6]^{3+}$.
R is true. In the spectrochemical series, $CN^-$ comes after $NH_3$ (… $NH_3$ < en < $CN^-$ < CO), so $CN^-$ gives a larger $\Delta_o$.
R also explains A. A larger $\Delta_o$ means a higher-energy, shorter-wavelength photon is needed for the d-d transition. That pushes the absorption into the UV.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 5 · Coordination Compounds

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Match List-I (coordination species) with List-II (oxidation number of the central metal).
List-I:
(a) $[Cu(CN)_4]^{3-}$
(b) $K_3[Fe(C_2O_4)_3]$
(c) $[Ni(CO)_4]$
(d) $[PtCl_2(en)_2]^{2+}$
List-II:
(p) 0
(q) +1
(r) +3
(s) +4
questions.explanation:
(a) x + 4(−1) = −3, so x = +1 (q).
(b) The complex ion is $[Fe(C_2O_4)_3]^{3-}$. So x + 3(−2) = −3, giving x = +3 (r).
(c) CO is neutral and the complex has no charge, so x = 0 (p).
(d) en is neutral, so x + 2(−1) = +2, giving x = +4 (s).
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 5 · Coordination Compounds

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: In the extraction of gold, the metal is dissolved by cyanide in the presence of oxygen and water and then recovered by adding zinc. Which of the following statements about this process is INCORRECT?
options: Gold passes into aqueous solution as the complex $[Au(CN)_2]^-$
Gold is present in the +1 oxidation state in the dissolved complex
Zinc acts as a reducing agent and gold is obtained in metallic form
Oxygen is needed to reduce gold so that it can bind cyanide
questions.explanation:
(1) Correct: gold forms the complex $[Au(CN)_2]^-$ in aqueous solution.
(2) Correct: $x + 2(-1) = -1$, so $x = +1$.
(3) Correct: zinc, being more reactive, reduces Au(I) and gold separates in metallic form.
(4) Incorrect: Au(0) changes to Au(+1), which is an oxidation. Oxygen acts as the oxidising agent, not as a reductant.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 5 · Coordination Compounds

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
How many of the following are inner orbital ($d^2sp^3$) complexes according to valence bond theory as described in NCERT?
$[Co(NH_3)_6]^{3+}$, $[CoF_6]^{3-}$, $[Mn(CN)_6]^{3-}$, $[Fe(CN)_6]^{3-}$, $[Co(C_2O_4)_3]^{3-}$, $[FeF_6]^{3-}$, $[MnCl_6]^{3-}$, $[Ni(NH_3)_6]^{2+}$
questions.explanation:
Inner orbital complexes ($d^2sp^3$), where 3d electrons pair up:
(i) $[Co(NH_3)_6]^{3+}$: diamagnetic $d^6$.
(ii) $[Mn(CN)_6]^{3-}$: 2 unpaired electrons.
(iii) $[Fe(CN)_6]^{3-}$: 1 unpaired electron.
(iv) $[Co(C_2O_4)_3]^{3-}$: diamagnetic.
Outer orbital complexes ($sp^3d^2$): $[CoF_6]^{3-}$ (4 unpaired), $[FeF_6]^{3-}$ (5 unpaired) and $[MnCl_6]^{3-}$ (4 unpaired).
$[Ni(NH_3)_6]^{2+}$ is $d^8$. Two 3d orbitals cannot be emptied, so it is also an outer orbital complex.
The total is 4.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 5 · Coordination Compounds

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the crystal field theory (CFT) is INCORRECT?
options: CFT treats anionic ligands as point charges and neutral ligands as point dipoles
The point-charge assumption suggests anionic ligands should cause the greatest splitting, yet they actually lie at the low end of the spectrochemical series
CFT fully accounts for the covalent character of the metal–ligand bond
In a spherically symmetrical field of negative charges, the five d orbitals remain degenerate
questions.explanation:
(1) Correct: CFT is an electrostatic model with ligands taken as point charges (anions) or point dipoles (neutral molecules).
(2) Correct: this mismatch with the experimental series is a known weakness of CFT.
(3) Incorrect: CFT treats the metal–ligand bond as purely ionic and ignores its covalent character. Ligand field theory and MOT address this.
(4) Correct: degeneracy is lifted only in an asymmetric (ligand) field.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 5 · Coordination Compounds

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Assertion (A): A square planar complex of the type $[MABXL]$, where A, B, X and L are different unidentate ligands, exists as three geometrical isomers.
Reason (R): In a square planar complex, each distinct isomer of $[MABXL]$ is fixed by which of the other three ligands lies trans to A.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true. NCERT states that square planar $[MABXL]$ shows three isomers: two cis and one trans.
R is true. In a square plane, each ligand has exactly one trans partner. A can be trans to B, to X or to L, and each choice fixes the whole arrangement.
These three choices give exactly three isomers, so R correctly explains A.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 5 · Coordination Compounds

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Statement I: In a coordination entity, the central metal atom/ion behaves as a Lewis acid.
Statement II: $[Ni(CO)_4]$ is a square planar entity while $[PtCl_4]^{2-}$ is tetrahedral.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Statement I is correct. The central atom/ion accepts electron pairs donated by the ligands, so it acts as a Lewis acid.
Statement II is incorrect. The geometries are interchanged: $[Ni(CO)_4]$ is tetrahedral and $[PtCl_4]^{2-}$ is square planar.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 5 · Coordination Compounds

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The complex $[Ti(H_2O)_6]^{3+}$ appears violet. According to crystal field theory, this colour arises because the complex:
options: absorbs blue-green light, which excites the single d electron from the $t_{2g}$ level to the $e_g$ level
absorbs violet light, which excites the single d electron from the $e_g$ level to the $t_{2g}$ level
emits violet light when an electron falls from the $e_g$ level to the $t_{2g}$ level
absorbs blue-green light, which pairs two electrons in the $t_{2g}$ level
questions.explanation:
$Ti^{3+}$ is a $3d^1$ ion. In the octahedral field, its single electron sits in the lower $t_{2g}$ set, and the $e_g$ set is empty.
The complex absorbs light of about 498 nm (blue-green). This promotes the electron: $t_{2g}^1e_g^0 \rightarrow t_{2g}^0e_g^1$.
The colour we see is the complementary colour of the light absorbed, which is violet.
The colour is not caused by emission, and the complex does not absorb violet light. There is only one d electron, so it cannot pair.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 5 · Coordination Compounds

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Match List-I (pair of compounds) with List-II (type of isomerism):
List-I
A. $[Co(NH_3)_5(NO_2)]Cl_2$ and $[Co(NH_3)_5(ONO)]Cl_2$
B. $[Co(NH_3)_6][Cr(CN)_6]$ and $[Cr(NH_3)_6][Co(CN)_6]$
C. $[Co(NH_3)_5(SO_4)]Br$ and $[Co(NH_3)_5Br]SO_4$
D. $[Cr(H_2O)_6]Cl_3$ and $[Cr(H_2O)_5Cl]Cl_2\cdot H_2O$
List-II
I. Ionisation
II. Solvate
III. Linkage
IV. Coordination
questions.explanation:
A: Nitrite is bonded through N in one compound and through O in the other. This is linkage isomerism (III).
B: $NH_3$ and $CN^-$ are interchanged between the two metal centres. This is coordination isomerism (IV).
C: Sulphate and bromide exchange their roles as ligand and counter ion. This is ionisation isomerism (I).
D: Water is coordinated in one compound and present as lattice water in the other. This is solvate (hydrate) isomerism (II).
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 5 · Coordination Compounds

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Match List-I (ligand) with List-II (description).
List-I:
(a) $N(CH_2CH_2NH_2)_3$
(b) $C_2O_4^{2-}$
(c) $NO_2^-$
(d) $H_2O$
List-II:
(i) Unidentate neutral ligand, named 'aqua'
(ii) Can coordinate through either N or O
(iii) Didentate dianionic ligand
(iv) Polydentate ligand
questions.explanation:
(a) $N(CH_2CH_2NH_2)_3$ has several N donor atoms, so it is polydentate: (iv).
(b) Oxalate carries a 2– charge and binds through two O atoms, so it is didentate: (iii).
(c) $NO_2^-$ is ambidentate and binds via N (nitrito-N) or O (nitrito-O): (ii).
(d) $H_2O$ binds through one O atom and is named aqua: (i).
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 5 · Coordination Compounds

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Impure nickel can be purified by converting it into a volatile coordination compound and then decomposing that compound. The compound is:
questions.explanation:
NCERT gives this as an example of purifying a metal through forming and then decomposing a coordination compound.
Impure nickel is converted into $[Ni(CO)_4]$ (tetracarbonylnickel(0)).
This compound is then decomposed to give pure nickel.
The cyanido, ammine and chlorido complexes are ionic species and are not used in this process.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 5 · Coordination Compounds

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Statement I: $[Cr(H_2O)_6]Cl_3$ is violet, whereas its isomer $[Cr(H_2O)_5Cl]Cl_2\cdot H_2O$ is grey-green.
Statement II: Solvate isomerism is a type of stereoisomerism because the two isomers have the same bonds but a different spatial arrangement.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Statement I is correct. NCERT gives the aqua complex as violet and its hydrate isomer as grey-green.
Statement II is incorrect. Solvate (hydrate) isomerism is a structural isomerism.
In one isomer, a water molecule is bonded to Cr. In the other, a chloride is bonded to Cr and that water sits in the lattice. So the bonds themselves differ.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 5 · Coordination Compounds

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Statement I: In metal carbonyls, the M–C $\sigma$ bond is formed by donation of the lone pair on the carbonyl carbon into a vacant orbital of the metal.
Statement II: The M–C $\pi$ bond is formed by donation of a pair of electrons from a filled metal d orbital into the vacant bonding $\pi$ orbital of carbon monoxide.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Statement I is correct. It describes the ligand-to-metal $\sigma$ donation from the lone pair on carbon.
Statement II is incorrect. Back donation from a filled metal d orbital goes into the vacant antibonding $\pi^*$ orbital of CO, not a bonding $\pi$ orbital.
These two interactions together form the synergic bond that strengthens the metal–CO bond.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 5 · Coordination Compounds

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Wilkinson catalyst, $[(Ph_3P)_3RhCl]$, is used industrially for which of the following processes?
questions.explanation:
NCERT gives Wilkinson catalyst, a rhodium complex $[(Ph_3P)_3RhCl]$, as an example of a coordination compound used as an industrial catalyst.
Its use is the hydrogenation of alkenes.
Purification of nickel is done by a different method, through $[Ni(CO)_4]$.
The other options are not processes NCERT associates with this catalyst.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 5 · Coordination Compounds

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following homoleptic metal carbonyls contains CO groups that bridge two metal atoms?
questions.explanation:
In octacarbonyldicobalt(0), the two cobalt atoms are joined by a Co–Co bond. This bond is bridged by two CO groups.
$[Mn_2(CO)_{10}]$ is also a dinuclear carbonyl, but its two $Mn(CO)_5$ units are joined only by a direct Mn–Mn bond. All its CO groups are terminal.
$[Ni(CO)_4]$ and $[Cr(CO)_6]$ are mononuclear, so they cannot have bridging CO.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 5 · Coordination Compounds

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: What is the total number of stereoisomers (geometrical isomers plus optical isomers) possible for the octahedral complex ion $[Co(NH_3)_2Cl_2(en)]^+$?
questions.explanation:
Step 1: The en ligand spans two cis positions. The remaining four positions hold 2 NH3 and 2 Cl.
Step 2: There are three geometrical arrangements:
(i) Two NH3 trans, two Cl cis. A mirror plane exists, so this isomer is achiral.
(ii) Two Cl trans, two NH3 cis. This isomer is also achiral.
(iii) Two NH3 cis and two Cl cis. No mirror plane exists, so this isomer is chiral and gives a d and an l form.
Step 3: Total = 2 achiral isomers + 2 enantiomers = 4.
The option 3 counts only the geometrical isomers and ignores the enantiomeric pair.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 5 · Coordination Compounds

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
$[Ti(H_2O)_6]^{3+}$ absorbs light of wavelength 498 nm, which promotes its d electron from $t_{2g}$ to $e_g$. Calculate the crystal field splitting energy $\Delta_o$ in kJ $mol^{-1}$.
(Take $h = 6.626 \times 10^{-34}$ J s, $c = 3.0 \times 10^{8}$ m $s^{-1}$, $N_A = 6.022 \times 10^{23}$ $mol^{-1}$.)
questions.explanation:
Given: $\lambda = 498 \times 10^{-9}$ m. The energy of the $t_{2g} \to e_g$ transition equals $\Delta_o$.
Formula: $\Delta_o$ per mole $= \frac{hc}{\lambda} N_A$.
Substituting: $\frac{6.626 \times 10^{-34} \times 3.0 \times 10^{8}}{498 \times 10^{-9}} = 3.99 \times 10^{-19}$ J per ion.
Multiplying by $N_A$: $3.99 \times 10^{-19} \times 6.022 \times 10^{23} \approx 2.40 \times 10^{5}$ J $mol^{-1}$.
So $\Delta_o \approx$ 240 kJ $mol^{-1}$.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 5 · Coordination Compounds

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Match the complex in List-I with the number of unpaired electrons in List-II.
List-I
(A) $[Mn(CN)_6]^{3-}$
(B) $[MnCl_6]^{3-}$
(C) $[Fe(CN)_6]^{3-}$
(D) $[FeF_6]^{3-}$
List-II
(I) 1
(II) 2
(III) 4
(IV) 5
questions.explanation:
(A) Mn$^{3+}$ is $d^4$. In this inner orbital $d^2sp^3$ complex, pairing leaves 2 unpaired electrons, so A matches II.
(B) Mn$^{3+}$ is $d^4$. In this outer orbital $sp^3d^2$ complex, there is no pairing, so it has 4 unpaired electrons and B matches III.
(C) Fe$^{3+}$ is $d^5$. In this inner orbital complex, pairing leaves 1 unpaired electron, so C matches I.
(D) Fe$^{3+}$ is $d^5$. In this outer orbital complex, there is no pairing, so it has 5 unpaired electrons and D matches IV.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 5 · Coordination Compounds

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Assertion (A): In a water sample, $Ca^{2+}$ and $Mg^{2+}$ ions can be estimated selectively by titration with $Na_2EDTA$.
Reason (R): The complexes that calcium and magnesium form with EDTA have different stability constants.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true: hardness of water is estimated by simple titration with $Na_2EDTA$, and $Ca^{2+}$ and $Mg^{2+}$ can be estimated selectively.
R is true: both ions form stable EDTA complexes, but with different stability constants.
NCERT states that this difference in stability constants is exactly what makes the selective estimation possible, so R explains A.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 5 · Coordination Compounds

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Match List-I (compound, as written in empirical form) with List-II (type of electrolyte its aqueous solution behaves as). Assume Co has a secondary valence of 6 and Pt has a secondary valence of 4.
List-I:
(A) $CoCl_3\cdot6NH_3$
(B) $CoCl_3\cdot5NH_3$
(C) $CoCl_3\cdot4NH_3$
(D) $PtCl_2\cdot2NH_3$
List-II:
(I) 1:1 electrolyte
(II) non-electrolyte
(III) 1:3 electrolyte
(IV) 1:2 electrolyte
questions.explanation:
(A) The six NH3 fill all six positions, giving $[Co(NH_3)_6]Cl_3$. It ionises to 1 cation and 3 anions, so it is a 1:3 electrolyte (III).
(B) One Cl is inside the sphere: $[CoCl(NH_3)_5]Cl_2$, a 1:2 electrolyte (IV).
(C) Two Cl are inside: $[CoCl_2(NH_3)_4]Cl$, a 1:1 electrolyte (I).
(D) All four positions are filled: $[PtCl_2(NH_3)_2]$ is neutral, gives no ions and precipitates no AgCl (II).
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 5 · Coordination Compounds

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Three complexes are given:
(P) $[CoCl_2(en)_2]^{+}$
(Q) $[Co(NH_3)_2Cl_2(en)]^{+}$
(R) $[Cr(C_2O_4)_3]^{3-}$
The correct increasing order of the total number of stereoisomers (geometrical + optical) is:
questions.explanation:
R: no geometrical isomers, but the complex is chiral, so it has d and l forms. Total = 2.
P: one trans form (achiral) plus a cis pair (d and l). Total = 3.
Q: two achiral geometrical isomers (Cl trans, $NH_3$ trans) plus a chiral all-cis pair. Total = 4.
The order is therefore R (2) < P (3) < Q (4).
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 5 · Coordination Compounds

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The correct IUPAC name of $Na_3[Co(NO_2)_6]$, in which each nitrite is bonded through nitrogen, is:
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Find the charge on the entity. Three $Na^+$ ions must be balanced, so the entity is $[Co(NO_2)_6]^{3-}$.
Step 2: Find the oxidation state of Co. $x + 6(-1) = -3$, so $x = +3$.
Step 3: The entity is an anion, so Co becomes cobaltate. N-bonded nitrite is named nitrito-N.
Step 4: The cation is named first, giving sodium hexanitrito-N-cobaltate(III).
Option (2) has the wrong oxidation state. Option (4) names the anion before the cation.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 5 · Coordination Compounds

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: An aqueous solution of a cobalt complex gives a white precipitate with $BaCl_2$ solution but no precipitate with $AgNO_3$ solution. The complex is
questions.explanation:
A white precipitate with $Ba^{2+}$ means free $SO_4^{2-}$ ions are present. They form $BaSO_4$.
No precipitate with $Ag^+$ means there is no free $Br^-$.
In $[Co(NH_3)_5Br]SO_4$, sulphate is the counter ion and bromide is inside the coordination sphere. This fits both observations.
Its ionisation isomer $[Co(NH_3)_5(SO_4)]Br$ behaves the opposite way: it gives AgBr and no $BaSO_4$.
Options (2) and (3) have free $Br^-$ and no sulphate at all.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 5 · Coordination Compounds

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Assertion (A): The thiocyanate ion, $SCN^-$, is an ambidentate ligand.
Reason (R): $SCN^-$ binds simultaneously through its sulphur and nitrogen atoms to the same metal ion, forming a chelate ring.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true. $SCN^-$ has two different donor atoms (S and N), and it can coordinate through either one, as in M–SCN or M–NCS.
R is false. An ambidentate ligand uses only one of its donor atoms at a time; it does not chelate.
Using two donor atoms simultaneously on one metal ion describes a chelating di- or polydentate ligand, not an ambidentate ligand.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 5 · Coordination Compounds

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Match List-I (metal carbonyl) with List-II (structural description).
List-I:
(a) $[Ni(CO)_4]$
(b) $[Fe(CO)_5]$
(c) $[Cr(CO)_6]$
(d) $[Mn_2(CO)_{10}]$
List-II:
(i) Octahedral
(ii) Two square pyramidal units joined by a metal–metal bond
(iii) Tetrahedral
(iv) Trigonal bipyramidal
questions.explanation:
(a) $[Ni(CO)_4]$ is tetrahedral, so it matches (iii).
(b) $[Fe(CO)_5]$ is trigonal bipyramidal, so it matches (iv).
(c) $[Cr(CO)_6]$ is octahedral, so it matches (i).
(d) $[Mn_2(CO)_{10}]$ consists of two square pyramidal $Mn(CO)_5$ units joined by a Mn–Mn bond, so it matches (ii).
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 5 · Coordination Compounds

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The two enantiomers of a chiral coordination entity are labelled d and l. This labelling is based on:
options: Whether the complex is high spin or low spin
The direction in which each form rotates the plane of polarised light
The colour of light absorbed by each form
Whether the ligands occupy cis or trans positions
questions.explanation:
Enantiomers are non-superimposable mirror images.
In a polarimeter, the dextro (d) form rotates plane-polarised light to the right. The laevo (l) form rotates it to the left.
The cis/trans labels describe geometrical isomers, not enantiomers. Spin state and colour have nothing to do with the d/l labels.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 5 · Coordination Compounds

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following statements about isomerism in coordination compounds is correct?
options: A tetrahedral complex $[MA_2B_2]$ shows cis and trans isomers
questions.explanation:
(1) Incorrect. These two compounds exchange the counter ion and a ligand, so they are ionisation isomers, not linkage isomers.
(2) Correct. The two compounds differ in whether water is bonded to Cr or present in the lattice. NCERT cites this pair: the violet and grey-green forms.
(3) Incorrect. All positions in a tetrahedron are equivalent, so a tetrahedral $[MA_2B_2]$ has no geometrical isomers.
(4) Incorrect. Only the cis form is chiral.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 5 · Coordination Compounds

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Match List-I (complex) with List-II (hybridisation of the central atom/ion):
List-I
(A) $[Ni(CO)_4]$
(B) $[Fe(CN)_6]^{3-}$
(C) $[MnCl_6]^{3-}$
(D) $[Ni(CN)_4]^{2-}$
List-II
(I) $dsp^2$
(II) $sp^3d^2$
(III) $sp^3$
(IV) $d^2sp^3$
questions.explanation:
(A) $[Ni(CO)_4]$: Ni(0) forms a tetrahedral, diamagnetic complex, so the hybridisation is $sp^3$ (III).
(B) $[Fe(CN)_6]^{3-}$: this is an inner orbital complex with one unpaired electron, so it is $d^2sp^3$ (IV).
(C) $[MnCl_6]^{3-}$: this is an outer orbital complex with four unpaired electrons, so it is $sp^3d^2$ (II).
(D) $[Ni(CN)_4]^{2-}$: this is square planar and diamagnetic, so it is $dsp^2$ (I).
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 5 · Coordination Compounds

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Statement I: $[NiCl_4]^{2-}$ is paramagnetic whereas $[Ni(CO)_4]$ is diamagnetic, although both are tetrahedral.
Statement II: Nickel is in the +2 oxidation state in both complexes; the difference in magnetism arises only because CO is a stronger field ligand than $Cl^-$.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Statement I is correct.
- In $[NiCl_4]^{2-}$, $Ni^{2+}$ is $3d^8$ with $sp^3$ hybridisation and two unpaired electrons, so it is paramagnetic.
- $[Ni(CO)_4]$ has no unpaired electrons, so it is diamagnetic.
Statement II is incorrect.
- In $[Ni(CO)_4]$, nickel is in the zero oxidation state, not +2.
- Its electrons pair up in the presence of CO, leaving no unpaired electron.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 5 · Coordination Compounds

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Statement I: The IUPAC name of $[Co(H_2NCH_2CH_2NH_2)_3]_2(SO_4)_3$ is tris(ethane-1,2-diamine)cobalt(III) sulphate.
Statement II: In the name of an ionic coordination compound, the number of complex cations and counter anions present in the formula unit is shown using prefixes such as di- and tri-.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
questions.explanation:
Statement I is correct.
- Three sulphates (total charge −6) balance two complex cations, so each cation is +3.
- en is neutral, so Co is +3.
- 'tris' is used because the ligand name ethane-1,2-diamine already contains a numerical locant.
Statement II is incorrect.
- The numbers of cations and anions in an ionic compound are never indicated in the name.
- So there is no 'di…cobalt' or 'trisulphate' in the name.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 5 · Coordination Compounds

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
How many of the following formula–name pairs are correct?
(i) $[Co(NH_3)_4(H_2O)_2]Cl_3$ : tetraamminediaquacobalt(III) chloride
(ii) $K_4[Fe(CN)_6]$ : potassium hexacyanidoferrate(II)
(iii) $[Pt(NH_3)_2Cl_2]$ : diamminedichloridoplatinate(II)
(iv) $[Ni(CN)_4]^{2-}$ : tetracyanidonickelate(II)
(v) $[CoCl(NH_3)_5]Cl_2$ : chloridopentaamminecobalt(III) chloride
questions.explanation:
(i) Correct: ammine comes before aqua alphabetically, and Co is +3.
(ii) Correct: the anion takes the Latin name ferrate, and Fe is +2.
(iii) Incorrect: a neutral complex is named like a cation, so it should be platinum(II), not platinate.
(iv) Correct: the anion uses nickelate, and Ni is +2.
(v) Incorrect: multiplying prefixes are ignored when alphabetising, so ammine comes before chlorido. The correct name is pentaamminechloridocobalt(III) chloride.
Three pairs are correct.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 5 · Coordination Compounds

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Statement I: $[MnBr_4]^{2-}$ has a spin-only magnetic moment of 5.9 BM, so it is tetrahedral and not square planar.
Statement II: If $Mn^{2+}$ underwent $dsp^2$ hybridisation, one 3d orbital would have to be emptied, leaving only 3 unpaired electrons.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
A moment of 5.9 BM means $\sqrt{n(n+2)} \approx 5.9$, so n = 5.
Statement I is correct. $Mn^{2+}$ ($3d^5$) keeps all five electrons unpaired only with $sp^3$ hybridisation, which gives a tetrahedral ion.
Statement II is correct. $dsp^2$ needs one vacant 3d orbital. Five electrons in four 3d orbitals give 3 unpaired electrons (about 3.87 BM), which does not match the observed value.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 5 · Coordination Compounds

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Anhydrous copper(II) sulphate is white, whereas $CuSO_4\cdot 5H_2O$ is blue. The best explanation is:
options: Anhydrous $CuSO_4$ contains $Cu^+$, which has a completely filled $d^{10}$ configuration
In the absence of water ligands there is no crystal field splitting, so no d-d transition occurs in the visible region
Water molecules themselves absorb red light and give the blue colour
Anhydrous $CuSO_4$ has no unpaired electrons, so it cannot absorb light
questions.explanation:
NCERT states that without ligands, crystal field splitting does not occur, so the substance is colourless.
In $CuSO_4\cdot 5H_2O$, water ligands around $Cu^{2+}$ split the d orbitals. The resulting d-d transition absorbs red light, so the salt looks blue.
When this water is removed, that splitting is lost, and the anhydrous salt appears white.
Copper stays +2 throughout, so $Cu^+$ is not involved. Water itself is not the coloured species.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 5 · Coordination Compounds

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: $[MnCl_6]^{3-}$ and $[Mn(CN)_6]^{3-}$ both contain $Mn^{3+}$. What is the difference between their spin-only magnetic moments? (Use $\mu = \sqrt{n(n+2)}$ BM.)
questions.explanation:
Given: $Mn^{3+}$ is $3d^4$.
$[MnCl_6]^{3-}$ is outer orbital ($sp^3d^2$) with no pairing, so n = 4.
$[Mn(CN)_6]^{3-}$ is inner orbital ($d^2sp^3$) after pairing, so n = 2.
Formula: $\mu = \sqrt{n(n+2)}$
Substituting: $\mu_1 = \sqrt{24} = 4.90$ BM and $\mu_2 = \sqrt{8} = 2.83$ BM.
Difference = 4.90 − 2.83 = 2.07 BM.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 5 · Coordination Compounds

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The hexadentate ligand EDTA$^{4-}$ (ethylenediaminetetraacetate) binds a central metal ion through which set of donor atoms?
options: Four nitrogen and two oxygen atoms
Two nitrogen and four oxygen atoms
Three nitrogen and three oxygen atoms
questions.explanation:
EDTA$^{4-}$ has two amine nitrogen atoms and four carboxylate groups.
According to NCERT, it binds through the two N atoms and one O atom from each of the four carboxylates.
That gives six donor atoms in total, so its denticity is 6.
Option (1) reverses the numbers. EDTA has only two nitrogen atoms, so it cannot bind through four N atoms.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 5 · Coordination Compounds

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Statement I: $[Co(en)_3]^{3+}$ is more stable than a similar complex containing only unidentate ammine ligands.
Statement II: Ethane-1,2-diamine is an ambidentate ligand because it can bind through either of its two nitrogen atoms.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Statement I is correct. en uses both N atoms at once to bind the same metal ion, which makes it a chelate ligand. Chelate complexes are more stable than similar complexes with unidentate ligands (the chelate effect).
Statement II is incorrect. An ambidentate ligand has two different donor atoms and binds through only one of them, as in $NO_2^-$ or $SCN^-$. en has two identical N donors that bind simultaneously, so it is didentate.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 5 · Coordination Compounds

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
How many of the following formula–name pairs are correct?
(i) $[Cr(NH_3)_3(H_2O)_3]Cl_3$ : triamminetriaquachromium(III) chloride
(ii) $K_3[Al(C_2O_4)_3]$ : potassium trioxalatoaluminium(III)
(iii) $[Ni(CO)_4]$ : tetracarbonylnickel(0)
(iv) $[Ag(NH_3)_2][Ag(CN)_2]$ : diamminesilver(I) dicyanidoargentate(I)
(v) $K_2[Zn(OH)_4]$ : potassium tetrahydroxidozinc(II)
questions.explanation:
(i) Correct: the complex is a cation, ammine comes before aqua alphabetically, and Cr is +3.
(ii) Incorrect: the complex is an anion, so the name must be trioxalatoaluminate(III).
(iii) Correct: the complex is neutral and Ni is in the 0 state.
(iv) Correct: the cation is named first, and the silver in the anion becomes argentate.
(v) Incorrect: the anionic complex must be named tetrahydroxidozincate(II).
That makes 3 correct pairs.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 5 · Coordination Compounds

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: In a coordination entity, the central metal atom or ion accepts electron pairs from the ligands. On this basis, the central atom/ion is classified as a:
questions.explanation:
Each ligand donates a lone pair of electrons to the central atom/ion.
A species that accepts an electron pair is a Lewis acid. NCERT calls central atoms/ions Lewis acids.
The ligands, which donate the pairs, are the Lewis bases. So option (1) describes the ligand, not the metal.
No proton transfer is involved, so the Brønsted description does not apply.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 5 · Coordination Compounds

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: $[FeF_6]^{3-}$ is an outer orbital octahedral complex of Fe$^{3+}$ (Fe: Z = 26). Using the spin-only formula $\mu = \sqrt{n(n+2)}$ BM, what is its magnetic moment?
questions.explanation:
Given: Fe$^{3+}$ is $3d^5$. $F^-$ is a weak ligand, so the complex is outer orbital ($sp^3d^2$) with no pairing. This gives n = 5 unpaired electrons.
Formula: $\mu = \sqrt{n(n+2)}$
Substituting: $\mu = \sqrt{5 \times 7} = \sqrt{35}$
So $\mu$ = 5.92 BM.
The value 1.73 BM would apply to inner orbital $[Fe(CN)_6]^{3-}$, which has n = 1.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 5 · Coordination Compounds

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Statement I: In fac-$[Co(NH_3)_3(NO_2)_3]$, each $NO_2^-$ ligand is cis to the other two $NO_2^-$ ligands.
Statement II: In mer-$[Co(NH_3)_3(NO_2)_3]$, no two identical ligands are trans to each other.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Statement I is correct. In the fac isomer, the three $NO_2^-$ groups occupy the corners of one octahedral face. Corners of a face are mutually adjacent ($90^\circ$), so each pair is cis.
Statement II is incorrect. In the mer isomer, the three like ligands lie along a meridian. The two end ligands of that meridian are opposite ($180^\circ$), so one pair of $NO_2^-$ and one pair of $NH_3$ are trans.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 5 · Coordination Compounds

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: A square planar complex has the formula $[MABXL]$, where A, B, X and L are four different unidentate ligands. How many geometrical isomers are possible?
questions.explanation:
Fix ligand A at one corner of the square. The ligand trans to A can be B, X or L.
Each choice gives a different isomer: (A trans to B), (A trans to X) and (A trans to L).
NCERT describes these as two cis and one trans isomer, so there are 3 in total.
The answer 6 is wrong because it counts all permutations, and many of them are the same structure rotated or flipped.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 5 · Coordination Compounds

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: According to NCERT, $[FeF_6]^{3-}$ is an outer orbital complex ($sp^3d^2$). What is its spin-only magnetic moment?
questions.explanation:
Given: $Fe^{3+}$ has a $3d^5$ configuration. $F^-$ is a weak field ligand, so no pairing occurs in this outer orbital complex, leaving n = 5 unpaired electrons.
Formula: $\mu = \sqrt{n(n+2)}$ BM.
Substituting: $\mu = \sqrt{5 \times 7} = \sqrt{35}$.
So $\mu \approx 5.92$ BM.
The tempting value 1.73 BM corresponds to $[Fe(CN)_6]^{3-}$, which has one unpaired electron.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 5 · Coordination Compounds

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
How many of the following complex species have a coordination number of 6 for the central metal?
$[Fe(C_2O_4)_3]^{3-}$, $[Co(en)_3]^{3+}$, $[Ni(NH_3)_4]^{2+}$, $[PtCl_6]^{2-}$, $[Ni(CO)_4]$, $[Cu(CN)_4]^{3-}$, $[Ca(EDTA)]^{2-}$
questions.explanation:
Coordination number (CN) is the number of donor atoms bonded to the metal, not the number of ligands.
$[Fe(C_2O_4)_3]^{3-}$: 3 × 2 = 6. $[Co(en)_3]^{3+}$: 3 × 2 = 6. $[PtCl_6]^{2-}$: 6. $[Ca(EDTA)]^{2-}$: 1 × 6 = 6.
$[Ni(NH_3)_4]^{2+}$, $[Ni(CO)_4]$ and $[Cu(CN)_4]^{3-}$ each have CN = 4.
So four species have CN = 6.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 5 · Coordination Compounds

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Violet $[Ti(H_2O)_6]Cl_3$ becomes colourless when its water is removed by heating. The best explanation according to crystal field theory is that:
options: $Ti^{3+}$ is reduced to $Ti^{2+}$, which has no d electrons
without ligands there is no crystal field splitting, so no d–d transition is possible
the single d electron becomes paired in the $t_{2g}$ level
the $e_g$ level becomes fully occupied, so no excitation can occur
questions.explanation:
The colour of $[Ti(H_2O)_6]^{3+}$ comes from a d–d transition. Its single electron absorbs blue-green light and jumps from $t_{2g}$ to $e_g$.
This transition needs the d orbitals to be split by ligands.
When the water ligands are removed, there is no crystal field splitting, so no d–d transition occurs and the substance looks colourless.
Option (1) fails because $Ti^{2+}$ would actually have two d electrons. A single electron cannot pair, so option (3) is impossible.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 5 · Coordination Compounds

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Platinum(IV) forms a series of compounds PtCl$_4$.xNH$_3$, in each of which the coordination number of Pt is 6. Which member would precipitate 2 mol AgCl per mole with excess AgNO$_3$ and conduct as a 1:2 electrolyte?
questions.explanation:
The coordination number is 6, so the sphere holds x NH$_3$ and (6 − x) Cl$^-$.
The total Cl is 4, so the number of ionisable Cl$^-$ = 4 − (6 − x) = x − 2.
For 2 mol AgCl, x − 2 = 2, which gives x = 4.
The compound is [PtCl$_2$(NH$_3$)$_4$]Cl$_2$, a 1:2 electrolyte.
x = 6 gives 4 mol, x = 5 gives 3 mol, and x = 3 gives 1 mol.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 5 · Coordination Compounds

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The red colour of ruby is due to:
options: $Fe^{3+}$ ions present in tetrahedral holes of silica
$Cr^{3+}$ ions occupying octahedral sites in the mineral beryl
d-d transitions of $Cr^{3+}$ ions that occupy positions normally held by $Al^{3+}$ in $Al_2O_3$
d-d transitions within $Al^{3+}$ ions of aluminium oxide
questions.explanation:
Ruby is aluminium oxide containing about 0.5–1% $Cr^{3+}$ ions ($d^3$). These ions are randomly distributed in sites normally occupied by $Al^{3+}$.
Each such $Cr^{3+}$ behaves like an octahedral Cr(III) complex inside the alumina lattice. The d-d transitions at these centres give ruby its colour.
$Al^{3+}$ has no d electrons, so it cannot undergo d-d transitions.
Beryl is the host mineral of emerald, not ruby.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 5 · Coordination Compounds

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: A 100 mL sample of hard water needs 15.0 mL of 0.010 M $Na_2EDTA$ for complete titration. All the hardness is due to $Ca^{2+}$, and $Ca^{2+}$ forms a 1:1 complex with EDTA. Express the hardness as mg of $CaCO_3$ per litre (ppm). (Molar mass of $CaCO_3$ = 100 g/mol)
questions.explanation:
Given: V(EDTA) = 15.0 mL, M = 0.010 M, sample = 100 mL, ratio 1:1.
Moles of EDTA = $0.010 \times 0.015 = 1.5 \times 10^{-4}$ mol, so moles of $Ca^{2+}$ = moles of $CaCO_3$ = $1.5 \times 10^{-4}$ mol.
Mass of $CaCO_3$ = $1.5 \times 10^{-4} \times 100$ = 0.015 g = 15 mg in 0.100 L.
Hardness = 15 / 0.100 = 150 mg/L = 150 ppm.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 5 · Coordination Compounds

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following is the coordination isomer of $[Co(NH_3)_6][Cr(CN)_6]$?
questions.explanation:
Coordination isomerism arises when ligands are interchanged between the cationic and anionic entities of different metal ions.
In the given compound, $NH_3$ is on $Co^{3+}$ and $CN^-$ is on $Cr^{3+}$.
In the isomer, $NH_3$ moves to $Cr^{3+}$ and $CN^-$ moves to $Co^{3+}$, giving $[Cr(NH_3)_6][Co(CN)_6]$.
Options (1) and (3) contain only one metal, and option (4) contains water. These change the formula, so they are not isomers.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Ch 5 · Coordination Compounds

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Match List-I (complex) with List-II (total number of distinct stereochemical forms possible).
List-I:
(a) $[Co(NH_3)_6]^{3+}$
(b) $[Co(en)_3]^{3+}$
(c) $[CoCl_2(en)_2]^{+}$
(d) $[Co(NH_3)_2Cl_2(en)]^{+}$
List-II:
(i) 3
(ii) 1
(iii) 4
(iv) 2
questions.explanation:
(a) Homoleptic with unidentate ligands, so no stereoisomerism: 1 form.
